To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the $\cos 2\phi$ azimuthal asymmetry is dominated by the linearly polarized and unpolarized gluon T-odd distributions, while $\cos 4\phi$ is dominated by the unpolarized gluons.

the azimuthal asymmetry of quark pairs in pA collisions is dominated by the unpolarized gluon distribution and that the linearly polarized distribution contributes at the same level as the unpolarized one.
the $\cos 4\phi$ modulation is sensitive to the gluon Sivers function, while the $\cos 2\phi$ modulation can be sensitive to the gluonic Boer-Mulders function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions.
the study of azimuthal modulations in quark pair production, in particular, the $\cos 4\phi$ modulation, in the correlation limit.

the azimuthal asymmetry of the quark pairs produced by the scattering of a proton and a nucleus in the framework of the hybrid approach, where the Lipatov equation is solved on the proton side, while the nucleus is treated within the color glass condensate framework.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the azimuthal asymmetry of quark pair productions is a powerful tool for probing the gluon TMDs in the proton and nucleus, and the nuclear modification of the gluon distributions in the CGC framework.
the azimuthal asymmetry of quark pairs is a sensitive probe of the gluon polarization in the proton and in the target nucleus.

the $\cos 2\phi$ asymmetry in the correlation limit is sensitive to the unpolarized and the linearly polarized quark-gluon TMD distributions, whereas the $\cos 4\phi$ asymmetries is sensitive to the linearly polarised gluon TMD distribution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the azimuthal modulations are dominated by the gluon TMD distribution $f^g_{\perp T}$.
the azimuthal asymmetry for the quark pair production is sensitive to the linearly polarized parton TMDs.
the azimuthal asymmetry in quark pair production can be factorized into the product of a hard partonic cross section, a CGC dipole cross section, and TMDs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the linearly polarized TMDs can only be measured at very high energies in pA collisions.
the $\cos 2\phi$ modulation is mainly driven by the linearly polarized unpolarized gluon TFDs, while the $\cos 4\phi$ one is driven by the linear polarized gluon distribution function.
, at leading twist, the $\cos 4\phi$ modulation is dominated by the linearly polarized TMD distribution $g_1^\perp$ while $\cos 2\phi$ is sensitive to $g_1$.
